changes.first_step_to_challenge: Check the passage from finite odd-level seeds and congruences to the global core using the assumed stable-range lift. The final row projections alone supply no such passage.
Check the common threshold in the level-two argument. It must control both the used tuples and the family size with the same constant at every eligible point.
Trace the passage from a rational crystalline comparison to the specific integral cokernel clause. The last constructor requires an explicit power of the lattice parameter killing the cokernel.
Follow the tie in the first output back to the Fontaine datum at the same prime, fields and index. Existence of an unrelated tie would not give that output.
Check that the cell masses and the change-of-measures factor refer to the very cells selected by support and bi-invariance. An untracked volume factor changes the unfolding identity.
Check the comparison of the given lowest-weight coefficient with the model coefficient on the entire unitary group, including the nonzero scalar used to transfer nonvanishing.
Check uniformity of the step-choice bound for all eligible word pairs. A bound obtained after choosing the two words would have the wrong quantifier order.
Check that the change of representative preserves the local matching relation after the kernel comparison scalar is inserted, with the same measures on both model integrals.
Check why the subgroup on which a witness is known has finite index and why its index is invertible in the coefficient field used for averaging.
Check the reverse implication on a finite test algebra with nilpotent kernel over its residue target. Testing only field-valued points omits the infinitesimal condition.
Trace the finite logarithms outside the exceptional Gram primes, then check the descent of both adelicity and degree from the common coefficient extension.
Check why both a chart section and its inverse extend over the model chart. Extending the first alone leaves a possible zero along the boundary.
Check the equality of the section cycle and the divisor cycle component by component, including the local multiplicity. Equality of their underlying supports does not suffice.
Check that the ideal detected by the pulled-back sections is the generic ideal in the Chow-form hypothesis. Then recover the original matrices from the inverse archimedean norms.
Check the kernel and image of each level of the evaluation map. The same endomorphism must act on these identified torsion groups for the integral comparison to apply.
Check the hypotheses needed to extend the generic isogeny across the complement of the open, particularly that the stalks of the normal model are domains.
Check the invariants of the graded twist both in degree zero and in every nonzero degree. These two inputs are used at different points of the argument.
Check the step lifting a fixed localized element to a representative that is itself fixed in the positive crystalline ring. Clearing an arbitrary denominator only supplies a representative.
Check that the hypothesis is imposed on every iterate. The integral divisibility lemma requires the entire family of vanishing theta values for the numerator.
In recovering the coefficient ideal, check both cancellations with non-zero-divisor hypotheses and the divisibility by the prime power in between.
Check the threshold at $p=2$. The source first weakens the valuation bound involving four and only then applies the uniform sharp-cokernel input.
Check the compact-dual volume-to-count implication at the exponent determined by the output list. The two fixed fractions must survive specialization to the test predicate.
Check the passage from integrality of a constructed row to the reference period assertion at the linked bundle point, retaining its pins and its lattice.
Check positivity of each step scalar on a common model of a nonzero row part and the assertion that the resulting parts span the tested space.
Check that the period identity and the deep-cover law refer to the same host, index and character as the specialization of the flat-degree theorem.
Verify that the real volume, class data and spectral instance refer to the row picked by the original selection at that family index.
Check the passage from the joined-row count to the weighted estimate with the row's own labels and the fixed positive counting constant.
Check nonnegativity of the entire error before replacing its inverse denominator by the uniform upper bound. Comparing the denominators alone does not justify multiplication.
Verify the character-set cardinality in the averaging factor and the logarithmic width at each image index. Equal cardinalities without pointwise identification cannot transport the main term.
Check the sign of the coefficient of the logarithmic count before multiplying the upper counting inequality. Check positivity of the total weight before cancelling it.
For an arbitrary regular character, prove that the minimal polynomial of its root parameter has degree exactly $d$. A degree dividing $d$ would allow labels of the wrong size.
Track the same quotient and both spanning conditions through the finite Fock subspaces and the product-form argument.

Check the enumeration of the excluded zeros when the cosine vanishes. In particular, zero itself is disposed of by its zeta value, while the first excluded negative even integer corresponds to the natural index zero.
Check the factors removed at imprimitive primes on the whole open strip, including points with real part below one half, before using primitive reflection.
Check that the zeta branch really covers zeros of nonpositive real part. The strip implication alone only covers the open strip.
Check which inverse character is primitive and why the exceptional argument one is excluded after reflection, even for a principal character of modulus one.
In the reflected case check simultaneously that the functional equation applies at $1-s$, the half-plane input applies there, and the cosine factor has no admissible zero.
Check the equality of the embedded coefficient readings in the second kernel series. It is needed for the admitted system to describe the comparison chain already chosen.
Check the two uses of the coupling-coset identity, on opposite sides of the transition. Reversing the adjacent representative in one use changes the kernel being read.
At the common grid threshold, check that the open, functional, small-prime and covolume assertions refer to the same strengthened extension.
Check that the reciprocity and norm bound survives strengthening the extension and has the exact norm predicate used by the all-row theorem.
Check the construction of the definite-row field after intersecting all its eventual hypotheses. The functional and covolume records must apply to the selected row on that same slot.
Check that the rank, twist, share, bad-place and exponent bounds use the same row, and that the lower-weight scale threshold precedes the point and its parameter.
Check that the base membership theorem and the nonempty Weil block both apply with the same origin, geometry and retwisting predicate.
Check that the transport of Galois preconditions and the two-prime estimate survives passage to the same strengthened row and hence the same family.
Check the geometric-tie field on the actual dependence extension. It needs the previously obtained divisor and tie records for the same reciprocity choice.
Check the production of a function with values in the embedded coefficient field. It uses both the square-ratio assertion and the denominator estimate for that same family.
Check the identification of section ratios in the constructed rational model with the original evaluation ratios. The isometry and uniqueness comparison must concern the same shifted metrized line.
Check the transition from the small-generated chart count to the normed chart count. The second bound needs the monomial shift and upper normalization for its own lattice.
Check the terminal resolution data for the reduced inverse image of the exceptional locus; recording smoothness of the resolved scheme alone loses that divisor condition.
Verify that the finite boundary list describes exactly the original boundary on each chart, and that the final reduced divisor is the support of the pulled-back ideal on that very sequence.
Check the passage from branchwise Lelong limits to the full divisor integral. The estimate near the exceptional set must preserve the local orders that become horizontal multiplicities.

Check the two quasi-inverse equations for the polarization and its return map, then verify triviality of the kernel on the constructed product. The existence of a retraction alone gives no such polarization.

Check that one twist and one nonzero multiplier control the entire upper inclusion for every power. A choice depending on the power would prevent direct application of the fixed-twist asymptotic bound.
In the reverse implication, check that the image of the differential contains every $p^2w$ in the original module, so factorization over the valuation ring yields the required functional.

Check that increasing the prime-specific constants to their maximum preserves the nonlinear middle term, and that the row at three uses the outside-small-set and factorization hypotheses it was constructed with.
Check that the constant in the abelian CM component estimate is chosen before the datum and its bad primes. Verify the union-of-primes bound for the same level as the selected tower.

Check that the finite family for a fixed split test is selected before the finite set of inert places varies, then check the permutation that transfers a singleton split-place match to the original global datum.
Compare the exact reciprocity specialization in `RowT` with the hypothesis of P013, including the above-prime alternatives, before reusing the same witness in the two argument positions.
Check the kernel-bound input to C3 for the same selection and the eventual rank bound at the actual host.

Check that the split and inert comparisons can be moved to a single global datum, with both the required subquotients and the inert Satake conclusion still belonging to the original datum.
Check the split rigidity argument for a candidate decomposition with matched Satake multisets. It must identify the original cuspidal representation after obtaining unitarity for every constituent.

In the transfer from two finite block lists to one finite product list, check the actual level subgroup and verify that strict comparison preserves both subquotients and fixed-space dimensions for every candidate.
